nodes.summary: Let $p, q, c$ be points of a pseudometric space $E$ and let $R_n$, for $n \in \mathbb{N}$, be the iterated metric center sets of $(p, q)$. We say that $c$ is the metric center of $(p, q)$ when $c \in R_n$ for every $n$, and every point $y \in E$ with $y \in R_n$ for every $n$ equals $c$.
nodes.title: Metric center of a pair of points

nodes.summary: The Scottish Book Problem 69 claim is false: there is a complete pseudometric space $E$ such that (1) for all $p, q \in E$ there is exactly one point $c \in E$ that is the metric center of $(p, q)$, and (2) for all $p, q \in E$ there is exactly one point $x \in E$ such that $q$ is the metric center of $(p, x)$, but there is no complete real normed space $F$ with an isometric bijection $E \to F$.
nodes.title: Mazur–Ulam Problem 69 refuted

nodes.summary: Let $p, q$ be points of a pseudometric space $E$ with distance $d$. The iterated metric center sets $R_n \subseteq E$ of $(p, q)$, for $n \in \mathbb{N}$, are defined by $R_0 = \{x \in E : d(p, x) + d(x, q) = d(p, q)\}$ and $R_{n+1} = \{r \in R_n : d(r, x) \le \operatorname{diam}(R_n) / 2 \text{ for all } x \in R_n\}$.
nodes.title: Iterated metric center sets
